orchards & forest gardens provide seasonal fodder,

Stocking Density = Days per Paddock/Cows per Acre


Stocking Rate = (Daily Intake per Cow × Grazing Period Length) / (Forage Growth Rate × Total Acres)

Grazing Demand = Stocking Rate × Intake per Cow
Total Forage Supply=(Pasture DM)+(Tree Browse DM)+(Mast Crop DM)+(Understory DM)
Forage Supply = Forage Growth Rate × Acres

pasture health metrics  
Forage Availability (DM per Acre) above 2000+ lb DM/acre
Forage Growth Rate (DM per Acre per Day) 200+ lb/acre/day
Residual Stubble Height (Inches After Grazing) 3+ in grasses, 6+ in legumes -> Taller stubble = faster regrowth & deeper roots
Soil Compaction  (Penetrometer Test) want Loose spongy soil that absorbs water well -> compacted soil = slower regrowth
cow grazing efficiency is ~60%

plant regrowth patterns
10 days Recovery Phase
10-30 days Rapid Growth Phase 200-300 lbs DM/day per acre
30+ days plants too fibrous = selective grazing

overgrazing: when cows eat plant in recovery phase leading to inefficiency
grass goes into depletion mode where in recovery phase root energy is depleted
in response plants do productive tillering producing worse quality DM

grazing impact
soil compaction: makes harder for roots to expand and water to be retained in soil -> weaker plants -> regrowth supression
80% open pasture (high-yield grasses & legumes for daily grazing)
10% tree cover (scattered) (shade, nitrogen-fixing trees like honey locust)
10% buffer zone (hedgerows, riparian zones)

✅ Mast Crops (Fruit & Nuts as Energy Sources)
Apples: 10-15 lbs DM/tree
Pears: 8-12 lbs DM/tree

Normally, forage growth rate per acre per day is 200-300 lbs DM for pasture alone. If you add tree/shrub fodder, the new forage availability calculation becomes:

Total Forage Supply=(Pasture DM)+(Tree Browse DM)+(Mast Crop DM)+(Understory DM)\text{Total Forage Supply} = (\text{Pasture DM}) + (\text{Tree Browse DM}) + (\text{Mast Crop DM}) + (\text{Understory DM})Total Forage Supply=(Pasture DM)+(Tree Browse DM)+(Mast Crop DM)+(Understory DM)

📌 Example Calculation:  
For a 5-acre silvopasture paddock, assume:
Pasture Growth Rate = 250 lbs DM/acre/day
Edible Tree Browse = 3,000 lbs DM/acre/year → (3,000 ÷ 365) ≈ 8 lbs DM/acre/day
Nut & Fruit Crop DM = 1,000 lbs DM/acre/year → (1,000 ÷ 365) ≈ 3 lbs DM/acre/day
Understory Clover = 1,000 lbs DM/acre/year → (1,000 ÷ 365) ≈ 3 lbs DM/acre/day

Total adjusted forage supply per acre per day:

250+8+3+3=264 lbs DM/acre/day250 + 8 + 3 + 3 = 264 \text{ lbs DM/acre/day}250+8+3+3=264 lbs DM/acre/day

Total Forage Supply=(Pasture DM)+(Tree Browse DM)+(Mast Crop DM)+(Understory DM)\text{Total Forage Supply} = (\text{Pasture DM}) + (\text{Tree Browse DM}) + (\text{Mast Crop DM}) + (\text{Understory DM})Total Forage Supply=(Pasture DM)+(Tree Browse DM)+(Mast Crop DM)+(Understory DM)

📌 Example Calculation:  
For a 5-acre silvopasture paddock, assume:
Pasture Growth Rate = 250 lbs DM/acre/day
Edible Tree Browse = 3,000 lbs DM/acre/year → (3,000 ÷ 365) ≈ 8 lbs DM/acre/day
Nut & Fruit Crop DM = 1,000 lbs DM/acre/year → (1,000 ÷ 365) ≈ 3 lbs DM/acre/day
Understory Clover = 1,000 lbs DM/acre/year → (1,000 ÷ 365) ≈ 3 lbs DM/acre/day

Total adjusted forage supply per acre per day:

250+8+3+3=264 lbs DM/acre/day250 + 8 + 3 + 3 = 264 \text{ lbs DM/acre/day}250+8+3+3=264 lbs DM/acre/day
